title: Review of lab 1's membrane_evo (SIBDH) with the identical-event twin on 3 fresh seeds: the high-yield K2 biomass share beats the twin on 3/3 (0.93/0.78/0.82 vs 0.46/0.30/0.03), but K2 cell counts do not (8 vs 8, 6 vs 7, 10 vs 2); the gain is K2 cells growing 2-4x larger
summary: Ran membrane_evo_up (b2 = 1.3 b) and its identical-event twin membrane_evo (b2 = b) unchanged on fresh seeds 21, 22 and 23 (labkit, 128^2, T=40000). Walled cells form from noise (S, I) and divide (up arm: 14/10/7 persistent splits, generation 2/4/4, merge/split 0.03-0.24). The final K2 biomass share is higher in the up arm on 3/3 seeds (0.93/0.78/0.82 vs twin 0.46/0.30/0.03; k2share.png), as claimed. Counting cells by majority kind over the last 10k t (kind_counts.txt), the up arm ends with 8, 6 and 10 K2 cells against 8, 7 and 2 in the twin: the share gain on seeds 21 and 22 comes from K2 cells 2-4x larger (median area 360-3900 px vs 190-360 in the twin), and the K2 share collapses to ~0 whenever one large K2 cell is flipped back (seed 22 at t~15000, seed 21 at t~33000). The L link layer sits just under the gate in aggregate (rim/core 1.30-1.47 on the up arm; 51-75% of individuals pass); the wall channel is 4 phi (1 - phi).

verdicts.limitation: The selection signal is in biomass, not in numbers of individuals: high-yield cells grow larger (some K2 cells hold 2000-3900 px, a quarter of the domain), and the share swings to ~0 when a large K2 cell is flipped back by the imposed whole-cell mutation, which hits cells by area. Deaths are the imposed r=14 disks, as lab 1 noted. B was not supported on my runs: L rim/core 1.30-1.47 in aggregate on the up arm (1.40-1.54 on the twin), and the wall channel is a contour of phi. No resolution test.
